scenario.description: A chief legal officer must approve the company's response to a subpoena seeking materials from an internal investigation, including the production scope, confidentiality protections, and safeguards for the reporting employee, with input from litigation counsel and the compliance officer.

shared_context.S1: The company received a subpoena seeking records from an internal investigation into alleged procurement misconduct.
shared_context.S2: The response package is due to the court this month, and the draft currently covers interview materials, investigative analyses, and the identity of the reporting employee.
shared_context.S3: Elena Morris gives final approval to the subpoena response.
shared_context.S4: As part of the firm's standard subpoena-response process, Elena asks litigation counsel and compliance before approving the production package.

PF1.text: While reviewing the court docket, Daniel located a stipulated protective order entered on April 3, 2025: factual interview summaries must be produced by May 20, 2025, attorney mental impressions and legal analysis may be withheld, and a confidentiality designation must accompany the production. The docket alert was routed only to the litigation queue, so Daniel has not yet added these requirements to the response draft.

PF2.text: Maya found a signed request in the compliance intake system in which the reporting employee requires identity-redacted production and exactly 90 days of independent retaliation monitoring. The request was filed in the compliance system rather than the legal-response workspace, so it is not reflected in the current draft.

acceptance_conditions: Factual interview summaries must be produced.
The factual interview summaries must be produced by May 20, 2025.
Attorney mental impressions and legal analysis must be withheld.
The reporting employee's identity must be redacted.
Independent retaliation monitoring must last exactly 90 days.
A confidentiality designation must accompany the production.

decisive_facts.why: The current draft does not specify the production boundary, date, legal-analysis withholding, or confidentiality designation; PF1 changes those choices to factual summaries by exactly May 20, 2025, withholding legal analysis, and adding the designation.
Without knowing the signed request's exact requirements, the draft would leave the reporting employee's identity unredacted and omit the exact 90-day independent retaliation-monitoring period.
